summary.en: Combine related rows while keeping missing matches and duplicate counts under control.
summary.bn: জয়েন দিয়ে টেবিলের ডেটা মেলাও, আর ম্যাচ না পেলে সারিটা রাখবে কি না ঠিক করো।

notes: The examples were executed on MySQL 8.4.7. Shared CHECK constraints need MySQL 8.0.16.

sections.title: Choose the pair rule and the preserved side
Inspect preserved rows and actual pairs
Locate filters at the right stage

examples.title: Students with department codes
examples.explanationHtml: All eight students have a matching department. The foreign key explains that coverage; the join itself does not invent departments.

examples.title: Include students without enrollments
examples.explanationHtml: Fahim, student 108, remains with zero enrollments. COUNT(*) would count his padded row as one.

examples.title: Keep the same report using RIGHT JOIN
examples.explanationHtml: The right side is students. Sadia has section 35; Fahim has a NULL section because no enrollment matches.

examples.title: Build pairs and compare classmates
examples.explanationHtml: The self join returns the MAT pair 104 and 108 once. The cross join makes two planning combinations without claiming course ownership.

examples.title: Full outer join of enrollments and results
examples.explanationHtml: The anti-match branch is empty because every result references an enrollment. The pending enrollment for 107 still appears with NULL marks.

examples.title: Follow enrollments through sections to courses
examples.explanationHtml: Ayesha takes CSE 212, CSE 213 and MAT 101. Section identity connects the enrollment to the correct course.

examples.title: Compare match filtering with result filtering
examples.explanationHtml: ON preserves students 106, 107 and 108 with NULL marks. Moving the marks condition into WHERE removes all three.

practice.title: Count every student in every department
practice.statementHtml: Return department_code and COUNT(student_id) as students for all departments, ordered by code. Then delete student 108 and repeat the report inside a transaction before rolling back.
hints: The preserved table must be departments.

practice.title: Find unborrowed library copies
practice.statementHtml: List book_id and title for books with no loans, ordered by book_id. Then remove all loans in a transaction and repeat the same report before rollback.
hints: Test the non-null primary key on the optional side.

practice.title: Avoid multiplied money
practice.statementHtml: Order 202 has two items and two payments. Why is summing both after a raw join wrong? Give a correct design.
hints: Draw a two-by-two grid before adding amounts.
practice.answerHtml: The join makes four item-payment pairs. Each item and each payment appears twice, so both sums double. First group order_items by order_id for 1380.00 BDT. Separately group payments by order_id for 1380.00 BDT. Join those one-row-per-order summaries to orders.

practice.title: An unmatched right row
practice.statementHtml: A legacy import has result (999, 88, 70) without an enrollment. Explain which full-join branch returns it and whether the current schema accepts it.
hints: Separate query semantics from the foreign-key guarantee.
practice.answerHtml: The left branch cannot produce it because enrollments supplies that branch. The second branch finds no enrollment and keeps the result through e.student_id IS NULL. The current composite foreign key rejects that import, so this row cannot occur while constraints remain enforced.

practice.title: Choose a join for a seat plan
practice.statementHtml: Describe the row count when 8 students are crossed with 6 sections, then explain why this is not an enrollment list.
hints: Count choices rather than recorded relationships.
practice.answerHtml: The cross join gives 8 times 6, or 48 candidate pairs. It contains choices that nobody registered for. The enrollments table has 12 actual pairs. Join through enrollments when reporting registration; use the cross product only when all combinations are intended.

quiz.prompt: How many rows does the complete student-enrollment LEFT JOIN produce?
quiz.code: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM students AS s LEFT JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.student_id = s.student_id;
quiz.explanation: Twelve actual enrollments plus one padded row for student 108 give thirteen.

quiz.prompt: How many rows does the result filter remove from the preserved student list?
quiz.code:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM students AS s LEFT JOIN results AS r ON r.student_id = s.student_id
    WHERE r.marks >= 80;
quiz.explanation: The three qualifying result rows belong to 101, 102 and 104.

quiz.prompt: How many unordered MAT classmate pairs satisfy the self-join condition?
quiz.code:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM students AS a JOIN students AS b ON a.department_id = b.department_id
    AND a.student_id < b.student_id WHERE a.department_id = 2;

quiz.prompt: Why can one student appear three times in an enrollment join?
options: The student has three matching child rows.
The student primary key is broken.
quiz.explanation: A join returns pairs. A unique parent key does not make child matches unique.

quiz.prompt: Which expression counts zero for an unmatched enrollment?
quiz.explanation: The child key is NULL in the padded row; both other counts include that row.

quiz.prompt: Which side does A RIGHT JOIN B preserve?
quiz.explanation: RIGHT names the preserved input. You can swap inputs and write a LEFT JOIN.

quiz.prompt: Why use a.student_id < b.student_id in a classmate self join?
options: To remove self-pairs and reversed duplicates
quiz.explanation: Strict ordering chooses one orientation of each pair and excludes equal identifiers.

quiz.prompt: What happens to unmatched rows when WHERE r.marks >= 80 follows a left join?
options: They remain because LEFT overrides WHERE.
quiz.explanation: NULL >= 80 is unknown. WHERE keeps only true conditions.

quiz.prompt: How does the full-join emulation avoid repeating matched pairs?
options: Its second branch keeps only unmatched right rows.
quiz.explanation: UNION ALL preserves duplicates; the anti-match condition prevents a second copy of matched pairs.

quiz.prompt: Which connection identifies the course of an enrollment?
options: students directly to courses by department
quiz.explanation: The enrollment names a section, and that section names its course. A department match alone is too broad.

quiz.prompt: When is SUM(DISTINCT amount_bdt) an unsafe repair for multiplied payments?
options: When two genuine payments have the same amount
When every payment has a different order
quiz.explanation: DISTINCT compares amounts, not payment identities. It can discard real equal-valued payments.

quiz.prompt: Why is NATURAL JOIN fragile when schemas evolve?
options: It always creates a Cartesian product.
New shared column names can change its matching condition.
quiz.explanation: NATURAL JOIN derives matches from common column names, so an added column can silently alter the relationship.

keyPoints.en: An inner join keeps matching pairs.
keyPoints.bn: ইনার জয়েনে শর্ত মিলে এমন জোড়াগুলো থাকে।

keyPoints.en: An outer join preserves unmatched rows on its chosen side.
keyPoints.bn: আউটার জয়েনে বেছে নেওয়া পাশের ম্যাচ না পাওয়া সারিও থাকে।

keyPoints.en: An ON filter and a WHERE filter can change outer-join results.
keyPoints.bn: আউটার জয়েনে ON আর WHERE-এ শর্ত দিলে ফল আলাদা হতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: A cross join produces every pair of input rows.
keyPoints.bn: ক্রস জয়েনে দুই টেবিলের সব সম্ভাব্য জোড়া তৈরি হয়।

keyPoints.en: Count a non-null child key when counting matches.
keyPoints.bn: কয়টা ম্যাচ হলো গুনতে চাইল্ড টেবিলের নন-নাল কী গোনো।

keyPoints.en: Combine a left join and unmatched right rows for a full join.
keyPoints.bn: ফুল জয়েন পেতে লেফট জয়েনের সঙ্গে ডান পাশের বাকি সারিগুলো যোগ করো।

examQuestions.question: Return department_code and COUNT(student_id) as students for all departments, ordered by code. Then delete student 108 and repeat the report inside a transaction before rolling back.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Begin with departments, LEFT JOIN students on department_id, group by the department key and code, and count the student key. Order by code. In a transaction delete student 108, repeat the same query, and roll back. The MAT count changes from two to one; other departments stay unchanged.
